title: Article 329A — [Repealed] Special provision as to elections to Parliament in the case of Prime Minister and Speaker

content.overview: Article 329A was inserted by the Constitution (Thirty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1975, and sought to place elections to Parliament in the case of the Prime Minister and the Speaker beyond ordinary judicial challenge. It was struck down by the Supreme Court in Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975) as violative of the basic structure, and was later repealed by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978. It is not part of the operative Constitution.
content.glance: Repealed. Inserted by 39th Amendment (1975); struck down in Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain; repealed by 44th Amendment (1978).
content.study:
Article 329A is historically important but inoperative:
- Inserted by the 39th Amendment during the Emergency period.
- Aimed at immunising the election of the Prime Minister and Speaker from ordinary election-petition challenge.
- Held unconstitutional in Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain as damaging free and fair elections / rule of law elements of the basic structure.
- Formally repealed by the 44th Amendment (1978).
